core.title: Keep every index-registry entry in sync with the document it indexes
core.given: A plan index registry artifact indexes individual plan documents by path, mirroring the mirrored fields declared by the stack profile from each document it indexes
core.when: the plan reaches the confirmation phase (CONFIRM), for every indexed entry, regardless of which files or fields the current change touched
core.then: every registry entry's mirrored fields must equal the values in the document it points at.
prefer: Treat the document as authoritative: edit the document first, then copy the mirrored fields into the registry entry in the same change.
When a mismatch is found — including a pre-existing one your change did not cause — fix the registry entry to match the document, not the other way round.
avoid: Changing the document to match a stale registry entry — on disagreement the registry is always the defect.
Updating a document's mirrored fields without updating its registry entry (or vice versa).
Treating an existing mismatch as out of scope because your change did not touch the registry or that document.
Adding fields to the registry that diverge from or are not sourced from the document.
core.why: The document is authoritative and the registry is only discovery metadata that denormalises the mirrored fields from it; any disagreement means the registry is lying to whoever discovers the indexed documents through it.
evidence: The registry-coherence check passes at CONFIRM against the live registry (all entries, not only changed ones).
On failure, the report names the indexed item, the disagreeing field, and the registry value and the document value for each disagreement.
verification: Disposition strict: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline. Severity 3.
Confirm-blocking: the check runs at the confirmation phase against the live registry and blocks the plan on failure.
Scope: every entry of the live registry is checked, not a diff — pre-existing mismatches count even when the current change touched neither the registry nor the document.
Only the mirrored fields are compared; differences in other document fields are not findings, and such differences never exempt a mismatch on a mirrored field.
On disagreement the document wins: the registry entry is reported as the defect.

fires: At CONFIRM, a registry entry disagrees with the document it points at on a mirrored field, even though nothing in the current change touched the registry or the document (a pre-existing mismatch).
At CONFIRM, after a planner added a registry entry whose mirrored fields differ from the document it points at.
At CONFIRM, after a planner changed a document's mirrored fields without updating its registry entry.
At CONFIRM, while the current change only edits unrelated plan files or non-mirrored document fields, but some indexed entry still disagrees on a mirrored field.
doesNotFire: At CONFIRM, every registry entry's mirrored fields equal the values in the document it points at (no finding, regardless of what changed).

Repositories with no index registry artifact at the profile-declared location; the rule is an existence gate — the registry must exist and index at least one document, but it does not need to be touched or read by the current plan.

Differences in document fields the registry does not mirror (anything other than the profile-declared mirrored fields) — these are not compared; but such edits never exempt a mismatch on a mirrored field.

profileRequirements.meaning: Path pattern of one plan document indexed by the index registry; each registry entry names one document of this shape by path, and that document is authoritative on disagreement.
Path of the plan index registry artifact whose entries mirror fields from the documents they index; its existence (indexing at least one document) gates the rule.
The concrete document fields the registry denormalises; exactly these fields are compared for every entry.

neutralityNotes: The core abstracts Bun's 'flow router registry'/'flow router document' into a plan 'index registry' and its 'indexed documents'; the kind name 'flow router' stays realization-side. The indexed-document path pattern uses the existing vocabulary key layout.plan_item (its DESIRED OUTCOME example is an example, not a restriction; under the Bun profile it resolves to plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers/*.yaml). Two profile keys remain proposed because the closed vocabulary has neither a key for the registry file's own location (layout.registries#index_registry) nor for the mirrored-field names (idiom.plan_syntax#registry_mirrored_fields). The phase name CONFIRM and the 'planner' persona are ATDD-process vocabulary rather than stack data, so they remain in the core. Severity 3, strict disposition and the confirm-blocking / live-registry / no-diff scope are kept in core:verification; this rule's validator id, validation-taxonomy ids (family/template/variant/subject_kind) and finding-report field names are bunOnly.
